root.claim: One deterministic fixed-tape Turing machine multiplies two $n$-bit integers exactly in time $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ with $\kappa=2^{-182}$.
root.method: Keep the transform-based multiplication of Harvey and van der Hoeven (Gaussian resampling, Bluestein chirp, synthetic polynomial transforms) but replace its two costly tape operations, address rearrangement and butterfly layers, by faster procedures obtained from rank-saving linear networks, then check exactness and total cost.

motivation.text: Scanning an array at every transform level costs $n\log n$ by itself, so a power saving needs both the data movement and the arithmetic of a level to be cheaper than a scan.

quote.quote: We therefore need savings in both movement and arithmetic.

root.salient: The saving is a genuine power $(\lg n)^{-\kappa}$ of the logarithm, although $\kappa=2^{-182}$ is astronomically small; the theorem trades constants and thresholds, not asymptotic order, for beating $n\log n$.
